description: Identifier of the study (one sampling event per study), event_0001 onwards. Links to host_occurrences and pathogen_mof.
Citation of the source paper: authors (year), title, journal and DOI.
Year the source paper was published. This is not the year of sampling, which is in eventDate in host_occurrences.

Type of sampling effort the paper reports for the whole study: trap_nights, sessions, time_period (a sampling period only), unspecified (effort described but not in one of these forms) or not_reported.
Total trap-nights for the study, where samplingProtocol is trap_nights; empty otherwise. The unit is trap-nights (sampleSizeUnit in the Darwin Core Archive).
Number of trapping sessions for the study, where samplingProtocol is sessions; empty otherwise. Study-level effort was poorly extracted, and this is filled for only one study.
Whether the paper reports data for individual animals (individual), aggregated data (summarised), or does not say (unspecified).
Level at which the paper aggregates its data: individual, site-session, site-season, site, session, study or unspecified; empty where not recorded.
Shared identifier for studies that report the same animals at different breakdowns that cannot be merged; empty otherwise.
Within a duplicate_group: primary (the finer spatial breakdown) or alternative_stratification. Keep only primary studies to avoid counting the same animals twice.
How the study's records were combined with, or separated from, another paper reporting the same animals.
Identifier of the host record, host_00001 onwards.
Study the record belongs to (sampling_events).
Host species name accepted in the GBIF backbone taxonomy; empty when the host is not identified to species.
Host genus in the GBIF backbone.
Host family in the GBIF backbone.
Host order in the GBIF backbone, which places shrews and moles in Soricomorpha and hedgehogs in Erinaceomorpha.
Host class in the GBIF backbone.
Finest rank to which the host is identified: species, genus, family, order or class.
GBIF backbone taxon key of the host at taxonRank.
Number of animals of the taxon recorded in this sampling session at this locality. 0 means the taxon was not caught; empty when the paper gives no count.
The same value as individualCount, with its type given in organismQuantityType.
individuals, or minimum number known alive for one compilation that reports monthly minimum numbers known alive rather than animals handled.

Sampling date, or interval as start/end, in ISO 8601. Dates are expanded to whole days whatever the precision reported; temporal_resolution gives that precision and verbatimEventDate the date as reported.
Country where the animals were sampled, as written in the extraction (for example USA). Where one state administers an area claimed by another, the administering state is used.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of country (alpha-2 in the Darwin Core Archive); empty for records that span several countries.
Name of the GADM 4.1 first-level administrative unit containing the coordinate, where the coordinate is precise enough to place it.
Name of the GADM 4.1 second-level administrative unit containing the coordinate, where the coordinate is precise enough to place it.
Name of the GADM 4.1 third-level administrative unit containing the coordinate, where the coordinate is precise enough to place it.
GADM 4.1 GID of the finest administrative unit named in stateProvince, county or municipality.
Latitude of the locality in decimal degrees (WGS84). coordinate_resolution_processed gives its precision.
Longitude of the locality in decimal degrees (WGS84). coordinate_resolution_processed gives its precision.
Host name as written in the source paper.
Site label or habitat description from the paper, where it distinguishes records at the same locality.
Sampling date as extracted from the paper.
valid; missing (no coordinate); or illogical (latitude or longitude out of range).

For a coordinate outside the GADM 4.1 outline of its stated country, its distance from that country's border: less than 50km or greater than 50km; empty otherwise. Every such coordinate was checked against its source paper (coordinate_reviews.csv).
Precision of the locality the paper reports: site, village, town, city, study_area, adm3, adm2, adm1 (third to first administrative level), country or unspecified.

Precision of the sampling date the paper reports: full_date, day_range_resolution, month_year, month_range_resolution, year_only, year_range_resolution, or publication_derived (the paper gives no sampling date; eventDate is empty, and publication_year in sampling_events is the latest possible date).
Trap-nights for this record as reported in the paper; empty when not reported.
How trap_nights_clean was read: trapnight_reported; nights (a value under 10, read as nights of trapping rather than trap-nights); or not_reported.
Identifier of the assay record, path_00001 onwards.
Host record tested (host_occurrences); empty when the paper reports results at a level that cannot be matched to a host record.
Study the record belongs to (sampling_events).
Pathogen tested for, at the finest name available (species, else genus, else family), followed by "detection".
Number of animals that tested positive.
individuals, or minimum number known infected for the compilation described under organismQuantityType.
Assay type: Serology, PCR, Antigen, Virus Culture, Sequencing, Western Blot, Serology and/or PCR (results pooled across both), Other, or Missing (not reported).
Number tested, the pathogen and assay as written in the paper, and extraction notes, separated by "|".
Pathogen species name matched in NCBI Taxonomy; empty when the record is not resolved to species.
Pathogen genus.
Pathogen family. A few records are for families other than Arenaviridae and Hantaviridae, reported alongside them; filter on this field.
Rank to which the pathogen is resolved: species, genus, family or unclassified.
NCBI Taxonomy identifier of the pathogen at taxonRank_pathogen.
How the pathogen name was matched to the ICTV and NCBI taxonomies.
Number of animals tested. 0 where none were tested by this assay (for example, where none were caught); exclude these records from prevalence.
Number of animals that tested negative.
Number of animals with an inconclusive result, where the paper reports it.
TRUE where number_tested is larger than the host record's individualCount (a check flag).
TRUE where measurementValue is larger than number_tested (a check flag; none in this release).
Pathogen name after harmonisation to ICTV binomial names, before matching to NCBI Taxonomy.
Pathogen family as recorded at extraction.
Identifier of the link: seq_00001_host or seq_00001_pathogen. A sequence linked to both a host and an assay record has one row for each.
Host record (occurrenceID) or assay record (measurementID) the sequence was obtained from.
NCBI Nucleotide address of the sequence.
host has sequence, or pathogen has sequence.
Host or Pathogen: whether the sequence is of the host or of the virus.
Gene or segment named in the GenBank record, where given.
GenBank accession as reported in the paper.
Primary accession returned by NCBI for query_accession; empty where the accession could not be resolved.
